nary_nodes.label: Third-place playoff
evidence: France vs England – World Cup third-place playoff: Prediction, kickoff
Who: France vs England What: FIFA World Cup 2026 – third-place playoff Where: Miami Stadium in Miami, Florida, the United States When: Saturday at 5pm (21:00 GMT)

A day before the world tunes in to watch the all-important final, France and England will play one last time in North America, hoping to end their disappointing campaign on a positive note – if there is one.

nary_nodes.label: Semifinal loss to Spain
evidence: Firm favourites to add a third World Cup title, in-form France were outclassed by stalwarts Spain in the semifinals

nary_nodes.label: Semifinal loss to Argentina
evidence: England’s agonising six-decade wait for a major trophy continued following a late, cruel defeat to Argentina.

nary_nodes.label: World Cup final
evidence: A day before the world tunes in to watch the all-important final

nary_nodes.label: Deschamps' last game
evidence: But Saturday’s contest has a good reason for them to put up another fight – it marks coach Didier Deschamps’ last game in charge of France.

nary_nodes.label: Golden Boot race
evidence: Captain and star striker Kylian Mbappe has the opportunity to take home the Golden Boot and match or break the tournament’s all-time scoring record.
Mbappe, the current Golden Boot holder, is second in this year’s race behind Lionel Messi, with both tied on eight goals, and the Argentinian’s four assists keep him ahead of Mbappe, who has three.

nary_nodes.label: Opta prediction
evidence: The Opta supercomputer has picked France as favourites to secure third place, winning the game inside 90 minutes in 50.7 percent of 25,000 pre-match simulations.

nary_nodes.label: Player injuries
evidence: William Saliba (back) and Brice Samba (calf) are unavailable for France, while England’s Jordan Henderson (wrist) is injured and Reece James (muscle) is doubtful.

nary_nodes.label: Expected lineups
evidence: (4-2-3-1): Maignan (goalkeeper); Gusto, Lacroix, Konate, T Hernandez; Zaire-Emery, Kante; Olise, Cherki, Doue; Mbappe
(4-3-3): Henderson (goalkeeper); Chalobah, Guehi, Stones, Spence; Mainoo, Anderson, Rogers; Madueke, Kane, Rashford

nary_nodes.label: Tuchel's disappointment
evidence: “None of our players and none of the French players want to play this match,” England coach Thomas Tuchel said after their loss to Argentina. “They want to play the final. We gave everything to achieve that. Everyone plays to win the World Cup, but that’s how it is.”

nary_nodes.label: Deschamps' acceptance
evidence: France’s Deschamps echoed the feeling, saying they have no choice but to show up.
“We’re not where we wanted or expected to be. The disappointment matches our ambitions, but we have to accept it,” he added.
